title: Affine-target monomorphisms from groups of multiplicative type
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme is an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams, and an $S$-group homomorphism respects these operations. Let $H$ be a commutative $S$-group scheme of multiplicative type of finite presentation: there is an fppf covering $\{S_i\to S\}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] and finitely generated abelian groups $M_i$ such that $H\times_S S_i\simeq D_{S_i}(M_i)$. Here $D_U(M)=\operatorname{Spec}_U(\mathcal O_U[M])$ is obtained by gluing the affine spectra of the group algebras $A[M]$ on affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U$; $A[M]$ has basis $e^m$, product $e^me^n=e^{m+n}$, and the group operations are given by $e^m\mapsto e^m\otimes e^m$, $e^m\mapsto1$, and $e^m\mapsto e^{-m}$. Let $G\to S$ be an affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], where affine means that inverse images of affine opens of $S$ are affine. Let $j:H\to G$ be an $S$-group homomorphism such that for every $S$-scheme $T$ the induced map $\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,G)$ is injective. Then $j$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The groups $M_i$ may have torsion; in particular $H$ need not be smooth.

proof.text: Refine the given splitting cover by affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ mapping into affine opens $V\subseteq S$. The fppf covering calculus gives a covering by these $U$, and its base change gives an fppf cover $\{G_U\to G\}$. It is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc], so [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion] reduces the assertion to all $j_U$. The scheme $G_V$ is affine by the hypothesis, and the affine fibre-product formula makes $G_U=G_V\times_VU$ affine. The split source is $H_U=D_R(M)$, and monicity persists: two $U$-points with equal images are equal as $S$-points and hence as $U$-points. Thus it remains to treat $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $H=D_R(M)$ and $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$.

proof.text: Let $\varphi:A\to R[M]$ be the coordinate map of $j$. Right translation $(x,h)\mapsto xj(h)$ defines an action on $G$. By the affine fibre-product formula and contravariance of Spec, its pullback is an algebra coaction $\rho:A\to A\otimes_RR[M]$: the action identity and associativity give the two coaction identities. Apply [lem-sfb-group-algebra-coaction-grading] to obtain $A=\bigoplus_{m\in M}A_m$. Write $c:A\to R$ for pullback along the identity section of $G$. Restricting the translation action along that section gives $j$, whence $(c\otimes1)\rho=\varphi$. In particular $\varphi(a)=c(a)e_m$ for $a\in A_m$.

proof.text: In $A[M]$ with formal symbols $t^m$, put $I=(a(t^m-1):a\in A_m)$ and $J=(t^m-1:m\in M)$. Clearly $I\subseteq J$. To prove the reverse inclusion take $C=A[M]/I$ and its universal $A$-algebra map $q$. The elements $q(t^m)$ are units, multiply according to $M$, and define $h\in D_R(M)(C)$. Let $x\in G(C)$ be the point given by $A\to C$. For $a\in A_m$, the action coaction sends its value at $xj(h)$ to $q(a)q(t^m)=q(a)$; finite homogeneous expansions give $xj(h)=x$ on every coordinate. Cancellation in $G(C)$ gives $j(h)=1$, and the assumed injectivity on $\operatorname{Spec}C$ gives $h=1$. Thus $q(t^m)=1$ for every $m$, so $J\subseteq\ker q=I$ and $I=J$.

source.place: Tag 022S, group law on all scheme-valued points; elementary universal-quotient calculation with the grading of step 2, written by Q69.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-graded-stabilizer-strong-products] to this $M$-graded ring and $I=J$. For every $m$ it supplies $a_i\in A_m$, $b_i\in A_{-m}$ with $\sum_i a_ib_i=1$. Applying the identity-section homomorphism gives $\sum_i c(a_i)c(b_i)=1$ in $R$. The element $z_m=\sum_i c(b_i)a_i\in A_m$ therefore satisfies $\varphi(z_m)=\sum_i c(b_i)c(a_i)e_m=e_m$. Every element of $R[M]$ is a finite sum of scalar multiples of these basis elements, so $\varphi$ is surjective. This includes the zero ring: the empty sums give its unique element.

proof.text: The affine criterion for closed immersions applies to $j=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$, since both schemes are affine and $\varphi$ is surjective. Thus each $j_U$ in step 1 is a closed immersion, and the cited fpqc descent gives that $j$ is a closed immersion. None of the grading, cancellation or lifting steps used smoothness or torsion-freeness of $M$.
